description: Bootstrap the explicitly user-authorized Abstraction Lock as a new dev_scripts toolchain capability, then integrate it immediately after Scope Lock.
planning_goal: Bootstrap one explicitly authorized new toolchain capability named Abstraction Lock under dev_scripts. Because this capability has no pre-existing architectural owner, treat its new module as the user-authorized bootstrap owner rather than requiring Patch Corridor to discover an existing application owner. Integrate that capability immediately after the existing Scope Lock in the canonical toolchain runtime, use it to enforce the established diagnostic/planning abstraction and bounded source-access grants, exercise it in onboarding, and preserve all existing toolchain authorities otherwise unchanged.

scope_lock.original_user_instruction: Fix it so that it works.
authorized_deliverables: Bootstrap the previously requested Abstraction Lock as an explicitly authorized new dev_scripts toolchain capability.
Integrate Abstraction Lock immediately after Scope Lock in the canonical runtime flow.
Enforce that lower-level source access requires an explicit bounded grant from higher-level toolchain evidence.
Verify the abstraction boundary in onboarding.
forbidden_expansions: Do not modify application, game, UI, system_bridge, runtime, or feature source code.
Do not modify GitHub workflows or repository infrastructure.
Do not build a ChatGPT/GitHub gateway plugin.
Do not redesign existing diagnostics, planning, propagation, FilePatcher, Scope Lock, or validation systems beyond the minimum hooks required by Abstraction Lock.
Do not perform unrelated cleanup or refactoring.
authorized_capabilities: Abstraction Lock enforcement inside the existing dev_scripts toolchain only

acceptance_criteria: The new capability owner is dev_scripts/abstraction-lock.mjs; no application/runtime feature owner is required or inferred for this explicitly authorized toolchain bootstrap.
Abstraction Lock returns deterministic machine-readable ALLOW, ABSTRACTION_VIOLATION, and ABSTRACTION_GAP outcomes.
The canonical toolchain evaluates Abstraction Lock immediately after Scope Lock and before lower-level repository investigation or mutation routing.

Existing generated intelligence and planning surfaces remain the default repository-investigation interface: Symbol Families, Dependency Graph/Watershed, Integration Surface Atlas, Runtime Signal Map, Effect Atlas, Native Contract Catalog, Patch Corridor, Corridor Context, Patch Staging, Change Propagation, FilePatcher, and canonical validation.
Generic repository/source search and guessed or ad-hoc source reads are denied by default for repository investigation.
Lower-level source access is allowed only by a bounded grant containing explicit path(s) and issuing higher-level toolchain evidence; the grant cannot broaden Scope Lock.
An evidence insufficiency returns ABSTRACTION_GAP and a specifically bounded permitted escalation rather than arbitrary exploration authority.
Onboarding verifies that generic search is rejected, guessed source access is rejected, a mapped/granted source path is accepted, and an unrelated source path remains rejected.

Existing Scope Lock, Patch Corridor, Corridor Context, Patch Staging, Change Propagation, FilePatcher, diagnostics, validation, mutation authority, and terminal-state behavior remain otherwise unchanged.
